images.filename: Quebec Monument - geograph.org.uk - 616487.jpg
images.caption:
Quebec Monument at Studley Royal Park — a landscape garden park in North Yorkshire. 
Garden feature known as the Quebec Monument which is dedicated to General Wolfe, who was successful in leading a British attack against the French fort at Quebec City on September 13 1759. The French were defeated, but Wolfe was shot in the chest and died just as the battle was won.
Wolfe's defeat of the French led to the British capture of the New France department of Canada, and his "hero's death" made him a legend in England at the time.
Nearby this monument is a small raised platform where a cannon was fired every year on the day of the battle to commemorate his victory.

Unfortunately this area is damp most of the year & consequently has become overgrown with comfrey & rushes, there is limited access to the public.

images.filename: A very Rustic Bridge - geograph.org.uk - 686528.jpg
images.caption:
A very Rustic Bridge Hidden in the woods of Studley Royal Park.
Located to the south of the Water Gardens, this "Rustic Bridge" is slowly crumbling away, not helped by the sapling growing out of the arch.
Tho it's a lovely spot for ferns.

images.filename: Mackershaw Lodges, Studley Park - geograph.org.uk - 1263294.jpg
images.caption:
Mackershaw Lodges, Studley Park 
"Gateway with flanking lodges, now ruined. c1740 for John Aislabie. Limestone rubble and ashlar.
Archway flanked by projecting single-storey 2- bay lodges. Round carriage arch with massive voussoirs and keystone (now with farm gate) flanked by flat-arched pedestrian gateways, now blocked, each with round-arched recess above ...
The lodges were occupied until c1970 ... The building stands on high ground and was probably intended as a focal point rather than an entrance to the park"
National Heritage List for England
